title: Adaptive Graph Refinement and Label Propagation with LLMs for Cost-Effective Entity Resolution

problem.claim: Dirty entity resolution identifies records referring to the same real-world entity within a single messy dataset.

gap.claim: The dominant blocking-matching-clustering paradigm suffers from critical flaws, including missing edges, noisy links, error propagation, and suboptimal clusters under rigid transitivity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Entity resolution is presented as a fundamental data management and mining task.
The dominant ER workflow is described as having critical flaws.
Its decoupled cascade creates a static sparse graph with missing and noisy edges, which propagates errors and can produce suboptimal clusters.

source_observation.claim: A cascaded, decoupled workflow can produce missing edges and noisy links that propagate errors into clustering.

interpretation.claim: Errors introduced in earlier pipeline stages may constrain the quality of later aggregation stages.

application.claim: When designing multi-stage entity-resolution systems, inspect how upstream blocking and matching errors affect downstream cluster formation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this issue occurs equally across datasets or workflow variants.

unknowns: The proposed method and its specific mechanisms are not described.
No empirical results, datasets, metrics, baselines, or quantitative comparisons are supplied.
No explicit novelty claim is supplied.
